newsitem.title: POLAND: IB Austria sees E.Europe dipping after bull-run.
newsitem.headline: IB Austria sees E.Europe dipping after bull-run.

text.p: East European markets are ripe for a correction after increased investment funds' presence in the region sparked a January bull run, which was not supported by fundamentals, Investmentbank Austria said in a monthly report.

"We believe that recent price rises, led by rising liquidity, have not been supported by fundamentals and hence a correction of up to 10-15 percent is likely within the next two to four weeks," the report dated January 29 said.
IB Austria said the region's markets benefited from the weak performance of emerging Asian markets and estimated that a total of $2.3 billion was pumped into the region in the last 12 months.
In the first three weeks of the year most of the funds flowed into Hungary and Russia, the report said.

It said it remained generally positive on the 1997 outlook even though large primary offerings such as banks, Poland's KGHM copper concern and Swiecie paper maker and Hungary's MOL oil firm could drain a large amount of funds from the secondary market.
It advised investors to go overweight in Poland, Romania, Croatia and Slovenia, to hold onto Hungarian shares, stay neutral in the Czech Republic and to avoid Slovak stocks.
